subject: Clarify IP carveouts & evidence handover schedule for Order Form
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@novasol.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up on IP carveouts and evidence handover for ProofHealth order form

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we prepare the PO and order form, Legal asked me to follow up on two items before we can sign: 1) carveouts around models trained on third-party data (they want explicit language limiting customer indemnity for pre-existing third-party claims), and 2) the evidence-handover timeline — specifically what logs/artifacts Redwood will produce if a third-party IP claim arises and how long those artifacts are retained.

I've attached a short questionnaire the team filled out with our initial constraints (customer_indemnity_questions.xlsx). We want to avoid open-ended cooperation requirements, but we also need a practical plan for evidence transfer if needed. Can you propose an internal owner and an expected SLA for evidence handoff? Also please note any changes to insurance thresholds we should expect.

Appreciate a short summary we can share with our Legal.

Best,
Elena
Sr. Contracts Manager, Novasol Health

Attachment: customer_indemnity_questions.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@novasol.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Follow-up on IP carveouts and evidence handover for ProofHealth order form

Hi Elena — thanks for the questionnaire and the clear ask.

Summary of what we propose (high level):
- IP carveouts: Redwood will accept a mutual carveout for pre-existing third-party claims that relate solely to the customer’s data or customer-provided training data. Redwood will propose specific language that narrows the customer indemnity to claims "arising out of customer's modifications or customer-supplied data."
- Evidence handoff: Redwood will provide a curated evidence package within 5 business days of a validated notice (logs, model version id, inference request headers for the relevant window). For deep forensics we will cooperate under a structured request process and can provide up to 90 days of retained artifacts subject to redaction of other customers' data.
- Insurance thresholds: standard request is $5M per occurrence / $10M aggregate for enterprise customers; we can discuss alternatives.

I've attached a redline of the Order Form (redline_orderform_v3.docx) with the language we think will be acceptable to both sides (section: Indemnity & Cooperation). Please review and flag anything that is a non-starter for Novasol Legal.

Next steps: can Karthik (cc'd) weigh in on the proposed carveout text and confirm whether the 5-business-day evidence SLA is reasonable from Legal's perspective? If so, I'll prepare a DocuSign-ready Order Form and a short mutual action plan with milestones.

Thanks — Hannah
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redline_orderform_v3.docx (document stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Elena Park <elena.park@novasol.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Follow-up on IP carveouts and evidence handover for ProofHealth order form

Hannah / Elena — quick legal note on acceptable carveouts and cooperation scope.

1) Carveouts: We can accept a narrowly scoped customer-only carveout limited to claims that: (a) pre-date the contract, or (b) arise solely from customer's use of third-party data where Redwood had no role in ingestion or training. We should avoid language that exempts claims that would otherwise implicate Redwood's model variants or deployment (e.g., model outputs that infringe irrespective of customer data).

2) Defense vs. reimbursement: Redwood prefers to retain defense control for claims that implicate our compiled model stacks, but we will offer a defend-and-reimburse compromise when the claim is demonstrably rooted in customer-supplied training artifacts. We'll propose a notice-and-evidence threshold (customer must provide prima facie evidence linking the customer's dataset to the claim) to shift cost.

3) Evidence handoff process: operationally, 5 business days for a curated package is tight but achievable for high-priority incidents if we have a named contact and an NDA/non-disclosure for any third-party materials. For forensic exports exceeding normal retention windows, we will need a signed work order and a cost estimate.

I'm attaching a short legal note with suggested clause language and a sample cooperation SLA that implements the 5-business-day window and the 90-day retention fallback. Please treat as internal draft.

—Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: legal_note_indemnity.txt (text stub)

Subject: RE: Follow-up on IP carveouts and evidence handover for ProofHealth order form

Thanks Hannah and Karthik — this is helpful. Novasol Legal has reviewed the redline and is generally comfortable with a narrow customer-only carveout as you described, provided we get: (a) a clear cooperation SLA (5 business days for a curated package, with escalation steps), (b) confirmation that Redwood will not withhold evidence on the basis of "other customers' data" when it is necessary to demonstrate the claim, and (c) a commitment to engage on a work order for extended forensics and a cost cap estimate if retention beyond 90 days is required.

Two small asks on the redline: can you add (i) a named Redwood evidence owner in the Order Form and (ii) a one-sentence commitment about timing to set expectations for our Security and Legal teams? If you can send a DocuSign-ready Order Form and the HubSpot record/DocuSign link, I can get internal approval and route the PO.

Elena
